target.title: fix(voice-call): consolidate webhook logs on the injected plugin logger and assert transcript privacy boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The voice-call webhook server (`webhook.ts`) was logging raw user transcript content and AI response text to bare `console.log`, bypassing the structured logging pipeline used by every other channel. Five log sites exposed caller speech content:

```ts
// Before — raw transcript content in logs
console.log(`Transcript for ${callId}: ${safeTranscript} (chars=...)`)
console.log(`Partial for ${callId}: ${safePartial} (chars=...)`)
console.log(`Auto-responding to inbound call ${callId}: "${userMessage}"`)
console.log(`Early AI response: "${text}"`)
console.log(`AI response: "${result.text}"`)
```

These are user conversation data — equivalent to message body content — that should never appear in plaintext log files. Other channels (WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, etc.) log only metadata (char count, message ID, redacted identifiers) for the same reason.

This is a follow-up to #103547 which addressed the phone-number leak in `events.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Consolidate all webhook diagnostics on the existing injected plugin logger** instead of introducing a second logging path. `VoiceCallWebhookServer` already receives the plugin's scoped `api.logger` through its constructor (passed from `createVoiceCallRuntime`). The module-level `createSubsystemLogger("voice-call/webhook")` would create a parallel logging path, allowing filtering, embedding behavior, test capture, and future privacy rules to drift between the two.

All 34 log sites in `webhook.ts` now route through `this.logger` — the single injected logger seam. The existing `sanitizeTranscriptForLog` helper and `truncateUtf16Safe` import are removed because transcript content is no longer logged — only `chars=` counts are recorded.

**Privacy boundary assertions** are added to the test suite via injected spy loggers that capture emitted output and assert:
- Call/stream identifiers and `chars=` metadata are present
- Raw transcript, partial transcript, inbound user text, early AI text, and final AI text are all absent from log output

## User Impact

- Transcript and AI response content is no longer written to log files. Only character counts are logged.
- All webhook diagnostic log calls use a single injected logger path, keeping filtering, redaction, and test injection consistent.
- No new public API or config surfaces.

## Evidence

- 48/48 tests pass in `extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.test.ts` (2 new output-level privacy boundary assertions)
- Reference: WhatsApp channel pattern in `extensions/whatsapp/src/send.ts` logs only `redactedJid`, `messageId`, `hasMedia` — never message body text
- No remaining `console.*` calls in `webhook.ts` (excluding the default-logger fallback block)
- No module-level `createSubsystemLogger` — single logger injection path through constructor

Behavior addressed: raw transcript and AI content removed from all webhook log output
Real environment tested: unit tests with injected spy logger capturing emitted output
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/voice-call/src/webhook.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: 48 tests passed, output-level assertions verify transcript/AI body text absent, `chars=` metadata present
Observed result after fix: transcript privacy boundary holds at the injected logger level; logger spy confirms no content words leak
What was not tested: live voice-call webhook flow with real Twilio/Telnyx provider webhook (requires real provider setup)
